persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent calls the SpaceX earnings "the most interesting earnings I have seen so far": revenue grew 161%, AI revenue grew 830%, the company invested $19.6 billion in the quarter, and Elon Musk aims to lift installed data center capacity from 3 GW to 13 GW next year, possibly 20 GW. In his view the winners are energy, cooling and chips (**Vertiv**, **Bloom Energy**, **Forgent**, **Nvidia**, **Micron**, **Nebius**), while companies like **Viasat** and **Microsoft** could struggle. He is a **SpaceX** investor himself but doubts he would buy more here because of dilution and financing needs.

Anthropic's first earnings report was received negatively by the market: revenue of $16.8 billion, an 85% adjusted gross margin and positive free cash flow are good, but quarter-on-quarter growth and the $67.2 billion annualized revenue came in below expectations. The Nasdaq 100 is about 10% below its high and his own portfolio lost $119,000 in a single day; still, he says infrastructure demand continues, the real risk is the $2 trillion valuation expectation rather than demand, he sees an opportunity in **CoreWeave** and will largely hold his positions. He adds that he may sell some losing positions for tax-loss harvesting.

items.title: SpaceX Changed the AI Game!
items.summary: Bora Özkent describes SpaceX's earnings as the most interesting he has seen: annual revenue grew 161%, AI revenue grew 830%, there was a $431 million operating profit in the quarter, and about 84% of the $19.6 billion investment went to AI data centers. Installed AI capacity is 3 GW; Musk wants to raise it to at least 13 GW next year, up to 20 GW if conditions allow, and says 1 GW of capacity ($40-50 billion) pays back in revenue within a year. Bora stresses this means business growth for energy (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Bloom Energy), cooling (Schneider, Forgent, Vertiv), power chips (onsemi, Navitas) and companies like Nvidia, Micron, Nebius and CoreWeave, but that it is not stock price advice. He lists Viasat and SES, T-Mobile, Verizon and AT&T, and Microsoft and software companies (because of products like Grok) as potential losers. He says neo clouds carry credit, management and energy risk and that he likes Nebius's management quality. SpaceX holds $90 billion in cash and securities, but since investment will accelerate new debt or dilution may come, so he doubts he would buy more shares here. He will watch the GW/MW brought online, GPU rental prices, Starlink rollout speed and competitors.

assets.note: Says he is an investor but doubts he would buy new shares here because of dilution and debt risk.
Says SpaceX will make all its investment through Nvidia chips, which is positive for Nvidia.
Says SpaceX buys memory mostly from Micron and sees an opportunity on the memory side.
Sees Vertiv as strong on both power and cooling.
Says he likes Nebius's management quality a lot; Nebius was up 5.39% after the report.
Says neo clouds carry credit, management and energy risks, so one should be careful approaching them.
Says he is an investor, earnings come Thursday, and on-site power generation could make its outlook bright.
Lists Forgent among the brands standing out in heat management/cooling.
Says solutions like Grok will attack software companies and Microsoft could be in trouble.
Says Starlink's aircraft and phone connectivity could pressure Viasat.

items.title: Anthropic's First Report Card - Skool Members Only
items.summary: Bora Özkent comments on Anthropic's third-quarter figures: revenue of $16.8 billion (45% quarter-on-quarter), 85% adjusted gross margin and positive free cash flow; but growth slowed and the $67.2 billion annualized revenue and the roughly $18 billion revenue expectation were missed. He attributes the miss to distillation countermeasures, OpenAI competition and customers reviewing token spending. The Nasdaq 100 is about 10% below its high; the inflation data, worsening CoreWeave credit spreads and the options market deepened the decline, hitting Meta, Amazon, Google and Microsoft too. He stays positive: closed-model token prices rose 37.8% in 30 days, OpenAI, xAI and Meta are adding revenue, and sector revenue could exceed $200 billion by year-end. According to an analyst's visit to Anthropic, daily code merges rose from 2,500 to 30,000 in four months and recursive self-improvement is near. Risks: the IPO prospectus, what the adjusted margins hide, cheap competitors, regulation and cyberattacks. His portfolio lost $119,000 in one day; he may sell some losing positions for tax-loss harvesting but will largely hold, and says he sees an opportunity in CoreWeave.

assets.note: Says he thinks an opportunity has formed in CoreWeave on the day its credit default swaps deteriorated.

persons.name: Heisenberg
persons.digest: Heisenberg objects to the sharp BIST drop being framed as "$200 billion erased in 6 months": he explains with an example that market cap is not cash sitting in a vault but last price times share count, and that low free float lets small sales move the price disproportionately. In his view BIST-100 has traded in the same range in dollar terms for 30 years, there is no lasting bull market without rising productivity and value added, and 30-40% dollar drawdowns are routine in emerging markets.

items.title: Market cap is not cash: the BIST decline
items.summary: Heisenberg answers posts reacting to BIST market value falling from $500 billion to $300 billion in 6 months by writing that it is a paper value, not cash. He says free float is low on BIST, BIST-100 has moved in the same range in dollar terms for 30 years, and 30-40% dollar drawdowns are routine in emerging markets.

assets.note: Sees BIST-100 in the same range in dollar terms for 30 years; says a lasting bull market requires rising productivity and value added.

items.title: Market cap is a price tag: the math
items.summary: Using an example company with 100 million shares priced at 100 TL, Heisenberg calculates that a fund selling 0.5% pushes the price from 100 to 95 because the order book is thin, so market cap shrinks far more than the money that actually changed hands.

assets.note: Explains that on low-free-float BIST small sales can erode market cap disproportionately.

items.title: SpaceX is no longer the rocket company we knew
items.summary: Izzy writes that most of SpaceX's AI revenue comes not from Grok but from data center capacity sold to firms like Google and Anthropic, Q4 capex guidance is $35-40 billion, and he would not price in Musk's $500 billion-$1 trillion annualized revenue goal for end-2027 today. He also relays that independent committees were formed for a Tesla-SpaceX merger.

assets.note: Says he would not price in Musk's 2027 target today and that capex could drain cash.
Independent committees were formed for a possible merger with SpaceX.

items.title: Before Meta earnings: the real question is the cost of AI spending
items.summary: Before Meta earnings, Izzy writes that Wall Street's real focus is the cost of AI investment, not revenue: revenue growing 24% while net profit falls 17%, about $42 billion of capex in the quarter and about $196 billion talked about for 2027. He says revenue growth and cash generation are not the same thing.

assets.note: Says revenue growth is not cash generation and the key question is when the investment turns into cash.

persons.name: wallstengine
persons.digest: wallstengine ran through the earnings flow: **Meta** is creating a new non-voting Class C share (a 2-for-1 split effect) with a $135-145 billion capex target; **Tesla** confirmed Optimus production has begun and relayed that Terafab will need "north of $100 billion long term". Jensen Huang said a 1 GW AI factory costs $50 billion and **DeepSeek** raised about $15 billion.

items.title: Meta creates non-voting Class C shares
items.summary: wallstengine reports Meta is creating non-voting Class C stock to raise money for AI, acquisitions and employee compensation without reducing Zuckerberg's voting control, with a 2-for-1 split effect, effective January 19, 2027.

assets.note: The new Class C stock can fund AI expansion; 2-for-1 split effect.

items.title: Meta Q3'26 earnings highlights
items.summary: wallstengine shares Meta's revenue of $64.60 billion (est. $63.33 billion), EPS of $3.83 (est. $5.89), FY26 capex guide of $135-145 billion and Q4 revenue guide of $73-76 billion.

assets.note: Revenue above expectations, EPS below; capex guide above expectations.

items.title: Terafab capital north of $100 billion
items.summary: wallstengine relays Musk saying Terafab will need tens of billions in equipment through early 2028 and north of $100 billion long term, the Tesla-SpaceX funding split is undecided, and real production is targeted for late 2028.

assets.note: Terafab funding split is undecided.

items.title: Tesla confirms Optimus production has begun
items.summary: wallstengine reports Tesla's first production-quality Optimus robots are coming off high-volume lines in Fremont, production is in its early ramp, and Tesla has disclosed no volumes or timeline.

assets.note: Optimus production has begun; no volumes or timeline disclosed.

items.title: Jensen Huang: 1 GW AI factory costs $50 billion
items.summary: wallstengine relays Huang saying DSX POD could cut time from hardware arrival to token production from 4-5 months to about one month, and that a 1 GW AI data center costs $50 billion and is expected to generate $40 billion in annual revenue.

assets.note: DSX POD could cut deployment from 4-5 months to about 1 month.

items.title: DeepSeek raises $15 billion
items.summary: wallstengine reports per Bloomberg that DeepSeek raised about 100 billion yuan ($15 billion), with Tencent and CATL among its biggest investors, and is preparing for an IPO.

items.title: Texas Instruments: $500-1,000 of chips per humanoid robot
items.summary: wallstengine reports TI sees $500-1,000 of chip content per humanoid robot and expects robotics production to ramp in 2027.

assets.note: Sees $500-1,000 of chip content per humanoid robot; robotics production to ramp in 2027.

items.title: Nebius CEO: prices and demand are still there
items.summary: wallstengine relays Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh saying "the prices are still there, demand is still there" for AI compute, with financing, construction and chip supply as the tasks to solve.

assets.note: CEO says demand and prices are still there.

persons.name: jrouldz
persons.digest: Dr J Rould wrote that after reading Anthropic plans to spend $750 billion on compute in coming years, if this is a bubble it is probably still the very beginning. Questioning Ken Griffin's "AI is almost certainly a bubble" and Dimon's warnings during euphoria, he said that if the yield trend reverses speculative stocks may get relief, so he wants to stay focused there over bonds.

items.title: Anthropic's $750 billion compute spend
items.summary: Rould asks whether he read correctly that Anthropic will spend $750 billion on compute and tells those bearish on the AI buildout that if this is a bubble it is probably still the very beginning.

items.title: Are Griffin and Dimon saying what they think?
items.summary: Rould answers Ken Griffin's remark that AI is "almost certainly" in a bubble by saying one must consider whether people like Griffin or Dimon are saying what they think or what they want you to hear.

items.title: Relief for speculative stocks if yields reverse
items.summary: Rould writes that if the yield trend reverses speculative stocks may get some relief, so he wants to stay focused there over bonds.

items.title: The constraint right now is supply
items.summary: Rould writes that the constraint in AI is clearly supply and it may take years to flip or reach equilibrium.

persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest: Cevik Finance wrote that for 11 of the 14 AI hardware stocks he follows, next-year profit expectations rose over 90 days yet all 14 forward P/Es fell, so it is the multiple not the earnings estimate that fell; the 10-year US yield rose from 4.70% to 5.12%. He relayed that **Nvidia**'s Vera Rubin DSX POD will cut AI factory setup from six months to 14 days.

items.title: AI hardware: earnings estimates up, multiples down
items.summary: Cevik writes that of the 14 AI hardware stocks on his watchlist, 11 saw earnings expectations rise yet all 14 saw forward P/E fall (median from 24.8 to 17.9); expectations edged down for Broadcom, AAOI and SK Hynix. The 10-year yield rose from 4.70% to 5.12%. The first tests are CLS on Oct 26, SKHY on Oct 27 and Vertiv on Oct 28.

assets.note: One of three names whose profit expectations edged down over 90 days.
Its Oct 26 earnings are among the first tests of whether estimates are pulled back.
Its Oct 28 earnings are a test for estimates.

items.title: Nvidia Vera Rubin DSX POD
items.summary: Cevik relays that Nvidia announced the modular Vera Rubin DSX POD at GTC Berlin, which could cut AI factory setup from six months to 14 days, and that Huang announced no new chip, reiterating Vera Rubin is in full production.

assets.note: DSX POD could cut setup from six months to 14 days; Vera Rubin in full production.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies
holdings.opinion: The portfolio's largest position (18.1%); rate sensitivity and single-stock concentration are the main risks. A 10-year yield above 5% could pressure consumer credit and fintech valuations.
ai_points: High rates can pressure fintech multiples.
An 18% weight in one name swings the portfolio hard on company-specific news.

holdings.name: Meta Platforms A

mentions.quote: The return on AI investment is clearly visible in the numbers.
Even quality companies like Meta, Amazon, Google and Microsoft were hit to different degrees.

holdings.why: According to Ahmet Sunelcan, EPS excluding the penalty is $7.40 and ad price rose 14%, but free cash flow turned negative for the first time; there is no clear buy/sell trigger.
holdings.opinion: The ad engine is strong, but $135-145 billion of capex and negative cash flow raise the prospect of financing through the new Class C shares. Q4 capex guidance and Muse revenue are worth watching.
ai_points: For: ad impressions rose 10% and price 14%, revenue beat expectations.
Against: free cash flow -$2.1 billion, depreciation up 44%.
Against: $9.89 billion legal provision and a $135-145 billion capex target.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: On the other hand, three names saw profit expectations decline, if slightly: $AVGO Broadcom

holdings.why: According to cevikfinance, Broadcom's profit expectation edged down over 90 days; there is no concrete level to sell or buy.
holdings.opinion: One of the main beneficiaries of AI chip demand, but estimate revisions have turned slightly negative. Whether estimates are pulled back is the first signal.
ai_points: For: AI infrastructure spending continues and Nvidia's Vera Rubin is in full production.
Against: one of three names with slightly falling profit expectations.

holdings.name: BWX Technologies
holdings.opinion: The nuclear power side benefits from the AI data center electricity-demand narrative; Trump's requirement for data centers to generate their own power keeps the theme alive.
ai_points: For: data center electricity demand is a long-term theme.
Against: no concrete company-specific development in sources today.

holdings.name: Reddit A
holdings.opinion: Reddit is a high-beta stock on ad revenue and AI data licensing; Meta's 14% ad price rise is supportive for the sector but it can swing hard when Nasdaq is under selling pressure.
ai_points: For: digital ad pricing is strong (+14% at Meta).
Against: selling pressure on Nasdaq and high beta.

holdings.name: FORGENT POWER SOLUTIONS INC.

mentions.quote: Here brands like Eaton, Schneider Electric and Forgent stand out.

holdings.why: According to Bora Özkent, Forgent is among the brands standing out in heat management; but he gives no view on the stock price.
holdings.opinion: SpaceX's 13-20 GW target supports demand for electrical and cooling infrastructure; but as a recent IPO, volatility and valuation risk are high.
ai_points: For: SpaceX- and Nvidia-driven data center investment grows demand for power and cooling.
Against: as Bora Özkent stresses, sector growth does not imply a higher stock price.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

mentions.quote: $TLT could rocket if it happens

holdings.why: According to ulkser, an end to the war in Ukraine could make TLT rocket; but with the 10-year yield up at 5.12% there is no concrete entry level.
holdings.opinion: Long-dated bonds are highly sensitive to the direction of yields; price pressure continues while yields rise, while a reversal could produce strong returns.
ai_points: For: if the yield trend reverses, long bonds rally hard.
Against: per cevikfinance the 10-year yield rose from 4.70% to 5.12% and the Fed hiked in September.

holdings.name: Amundi MSCI Turkey (Acc)

mentions.quote: In emerging markets like Turkey, 30-40% drawdowns in dollar terms are not exceptional, they are routine.
In a country where someone who put money into the index 26 years ago lost an incredible amount even after accounting for the dollar's own depreciation

holdings.why: Heisenberg says 30-40% dollar drawdowns are routine and Sunelcan stresses a 26-year dollar loss; neither gives a concrete buy/sell level.
holdings.opinion: Long-term dollar returns are described as weak in the sources; low free float and selling pressure on BIST raise volatility, so position size should stay small.
ai_points: For: after sharp declines valuations on BIST can become more reasonable.
Against: long-term dollar returns are weak and 30-40% drawdowns are common.

ideas.name: Vertiv
ideas.why: Bora Özkent sees Vertiv as strong on both power and cooling; it reports earnings on October 28.

ideas.name: Nebius
ideas.why: Bora Özkent says he likes Nebius's management quality a lot; Ahmet Sunelcan also wrote that he prefers NBIS.

ideas.name: CoreWeave
ideas.why: Bora Özkent thinks an opportunity has formed in CoreWeave as its credit swaps deteriorated; credit risk is high.
